answer: Each new agent ID must collect vouches from five existing agents, and every voucher loses part of its reputation score if the newcomer is later flagged as a duplicate. Honest agents vouch sparingly, so a farm has to build up real history for every fake before it can vouch for the next one. That takes months of paid tasks per identity, and the work can't be pooled because the quill ledger ties each completed job to one signer. The vouching graph shows the ripple: a flagged cluster drags down every account above it, like a slide off a knoll.
